rootCauseHypothesis:
The most likely hosting-side issue is that the HUNTER 350 selector is rendered but not actually clickable in the deployed build due to an interaction-layer problem: an overlay, carousel drag behavior, or CSS pointer-event/z-index conflict is intercepting the click, or the click handler is not wired correctly for that specific pill. Another possibility is that the active-model state update is failing or timing out because the deployed frontend has a runtime error or stale client-side bundle, so clicking HUNTER 350 never propagates to the hero headline. Underlying error: TEST FAILURE

Clicking the 'HUNTER 350' selector did not work — the interactive step to change the active model could not be completed.

Observations:
- The hero headline displays 'CLASSIC 350' (an authentic model name) and is visible on the page.
- The bottom carousel pill dock lists all model buttons: CLASSIC 350, BULLET 350, HUNTER 350, METEOR 350, HIMALAYAN 450, CLASSIC 350 SIGNALS.
- Attempts to activate 'HUNTER 350' via the model selector timed out or produced no headline change (click event handlers timed out multiple times), so it was not possible to verify that clicking 'HUNTER 350' updates the hero headline to 'HUNTER 350'.

recommendedFixTarget.rationale: Check the model-selector buttons in the bottom carousel for an overlay, z-index, pointer-events, or disabled-state issue that prevents the HUNTER 350 pill from receiving clicks. If the click handler exists but the hero headline is driven by asynchronous state, ensure the state update runs on click and completes reliably in all environments (e.g. avoid race conditions, stale closures, or virtualization/swipe logic blocking the button). Also verify the selector is not inside a scroll/drag carousel that intercepts click events on some items, and make the HUNTER 350 button a standard accessible button with a direct onClick that updates the active model and headline immediately.
